fact: leFaso.net reports that the BCEAO's PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform, launched 30 September 2025, connects banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions, with 80 connected by 24 June 2026.
Mixx Togo is a mobile wallet that its operator says has over 5 million users, 31,000 agents and 26,000 merchants in Togo.

Mixx users can send and receive money between mobile wallets, banks and microfinance institutions in the eight UEMOA countries through the BCEAO's PI-SPI platform, with an interoperable merchant QR code.

PI-SPI lets banks, e-money institutions, microfinance institutions and payment institutions transact instantly across the WAEMU; 80 are connected including 59 banks and 9 e-money institutions (Togo First).
Togo First says PI-SPI gives instant 24/7 transfers between banks, microfinance institutions, e-money issuers and payment institutions, and six Togo institutions are authorised to offer it.
Le Nouveau Reporter reports that Moov Money and Mixx by Yas mobile money are in service in Togo, charging 280 and 300 FCFA to withdraw 10,000 FCFA.
The article says Mobile Money is used for transfers, bill payment and services, and CGAR pensions were paid by Mobile Money in July 2026.

Togo First reports that Togo had nearly 4.96 million mobile money subscribers at end September 2025, and that Mixx (YAS Togo) and Flooz (Moov Africa Togo) operate the market per ARCEP data, with Moov launching insurance payments, card-less withdrawal transfers and gift cards on 7 July 2026.

Togo had 12.55 million e-money accounts, 6.07 million active (48.35%), at the end of 2024, with over 81,000 service points and nearly 5,800 merchants accepting e-payments, per the BCEAO report cited by Togo First.
PI-SPI is said to allow real-time transactions between banks, mobile money operators and financial institutions in Togo, though its adoption remains very gradual, per Togo First.
TechCabal says 36% of Togolese adults use mobile money and mobile money transactions reached US$1.54 billion in the first quarter of 2024.
Togo First reports Gozem Money, a mobile money wallet developed by Gozem with NSIA Banque, officially in service since 7 October 2025, alongside existing Flooz and Mix by Yas.
Gozem says users can transfer between operators and recharge the wallet from a bank account, with interoperability with card and other mobile money platforms in Togo.
CFE director Samuel Sanwogou says firms have been able to pay registration fees through Flooz and Tmoney online payment means since February 2019.
